topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: SIMD applies one instruction to multiple data lanes. It can accelerate suitable arithmetic when data layout, dependencies, alignment, and numerical semantics permit it. The worked example provides a portable scalar path and an x86 SSE path selected at compilation, with complete tail handling and no assumption that every machine supports a newer optional instruction set.

topics.summary: A vector instruction operates on several lanes according to an instruction’s semantics. This is distinct from creating several operating-system threads. topics.title: 17.1.2 Understanding SIMD Register Widths
topics.summary: Instruction-set families define different vector widths and supported element operations. A binary compiled for an optional ISA must not execute unsupported instructions on an older deployment processor. Compile-time selection is sufficient only when the deployment baseline guarantees that ISA.

topics.title: 17.2.1 Writing Auto-Vectorizable Loops
topics.summary: Simple contiguous loops with clear bounds and independent iterations are good candidates for automatic vectorization. Hidden aliasing, function calls, irregular control flow, or loop-carried dependencies can obstruct it. A compiler report can explain a particular decision, but the report must match the actual optimization flags and target.
